messages.content: Help me generate a DMG setup script for an application named 'PhotoEditor' located at '/Applications/PhotoEditor.app', with a custom background image and ensuring the script reflects the correct volume URL and installation directory when creating a macOS package using jpackage?

function.name: MacDmgBundler_prepareDMGSetupScript
function.description: Prepares a DMG setup script for a macOS application package, including the volume URL, background image file, and installation directory. Note that the provided function is in Java 8 SDK syntax.

appLocation.description: The file system path string to the application location. This is Java String type parameter in string representation.

params.description: A map of parameters that may include the application name, images root, background image folder, and other packaging parameters. This is Java HashMap type parameter in string representation.

We need to call the function MacDmgBundler_prepareDMGSetupScript with appLocation '/Applications/PhotoEditor.app' and params containing application name, images root, background image folder, etc. We need to provide JSON string representation of a Java HashMap. The function expects a string representation of a Java HashMap. So we need to pass something like '{"applicationName":"PhotoEditor","imagesRoot":"/path/to/images","backgroundImageFolder":"custom_bg"}' or similar. But we need to ensure it includes the necessary keys: application name, images root, background image folder, maybe others. The user wants a DMG setup script for PhotoEditor located at /Applications/PhotoEditor.app, with a custom background image and ensuring the script reflects the correct volume URL and installation directory when creating a macOS package using jpackage.

Thus we should produce a JSON string representing a HashMap with keys: "applicationName", "appLocation" maybe not needed because we pass separately. Also "imagesRoot" maybe path to images root. "backgroundImageFolder" maybe path to background image folder. Possibly "volumeURL" and "installDir". But the function will prepare the script based on these parameters. We can include "volumeURL":"file:///Volumes/PhotoEditor" or something. But we don't know the exact values. We can set placeholders.

We need to output the result of calling the function. According to instructions, we should call the function via the 'functions' tool. So we need to produce a JSON object with keys appLocation and params. The params value should be a string representation of a Java HashMap. That means we need to produce a string like '{"key1":"value1","key2":"value2"}'.

Thus we do:

{
  "appLocation": "/Applications/PhotoEditor.app",
  "params": "{\"applicationName\":\"PhotoEditor\",\"imagesRoot\":\"/path/to/images\",\"backgroundImageFolder\":\"custom_bg\"}"
}

But we might also include "volumeURL":"file:///Volumes/PhotoEditor" and "installDir":"/Applications". But the function likely uses the appLocation to determine install dir. But we can include "installDir":"/Applications".

Thus final JSON:

{
  "appLocation": "/Applications/PhotoEditor.app",
  "params": "{\"applicationName\":\"PhotoEditor\",\"imagesRoot\":\"/path/to/images\",\"backgroundImageFolder\":\"custom_bg\",\"volumeURL\":\"file:///Volumes/PhotoEditor\",\"installDir\":\"/Applications\"}"
}
